newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 2.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading.

* Views of traders and analysts were mixed on how the market will perform on Wednesday. Shares are likely to post a slight rebound on the back of the Dow's advance, says Erwin Tan, research manager at Abacus Securities Corp.
* Dharmala Securities economist Manuel Goseco, on the other hand, sees the market continuing its downward trek although not as sharply as on Tuesday due to the Dow's unconvincing gain.
* The Dow Jones snapped out of two-day selldown, closing 27.57 points higher on Tuesday at 6,611.05. PLDT's ADR rose by $0-1/4 to $60-1/8.
* Dharmala's Goseco said the market also awaits the release of February inflation figures. "As long as it's below 5.2 percent, then it will have a neutral effect on the market," Goseco added.
* Traders see the market's support at 3,100 points.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index fell 51.19 points to 3,171.79.
* Petron Corp's market share slipped to 42.4 percent in the first two months of this year, against 42.7 percent in the same period last year.
* Times Journal says the Central Bank reported a 34 percent drop in net foreign investments in 1996 to $1.055 billion from $1.61 billion in 1995.
* Manila Times quotes Economic Planning Minister Cielito Habito as saying the average inflation rate in March will likely stay at 4.4 percemt.
* Mabuhay Holdings Corp said it has increased its equity stake in Interport Resources Corp from 32 percent to 43.6 percent.
* Initial public offering of Premiere Entertainment Productions Inc starts today involving 180 million shares at one peso apiece.
* The peso closed lower at 26.367 to the dollar vs 26.363.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 8.9375 percent.
